resources.string: Looks like you\'re indoors. We suggest logging on the trail: it keeps where you live out of the data, and it measures the signal where people will need it.
Pressing %1$s records samples and shares them: what is recorded is sent to our server. No sample is recorded until you press %1$s, and recording stops when you press %2$s.

Each sample holds the position and time, the location\'s accuracy and altitude, and for each SIM its carrier, service state, signal readings and the IDs of the cell towers it hears. It also carries a random app ID made on this phone and a random ID for each recording. A sample never holds your name, phone number, accounts, IMEI or Android ID.

Samples are sent automatically when logging stops and when you open the app. Without a connection, the app keeps trying until they are sent, and until then they stay on this phone. On our server they are private and never published. Once our upload server is running, each sample will be deleted 90 days after it arrives; until then, samples on the server are not deleted automatically.

To send samples, the app connects to Firebase, the Google service that receives them, and signs in there with an anonymous account made for the app on this phone; Firebase keeps that account\'s random ID and sign-in times. Every connection shows Google the phone\'s IP address, and the Firebase libraries also send the phone\'s language and country setting and codes for its brand, model and Android version. The app also asks Google Play to confirm that it is the real app, on a real phone.
The samples themselves are not anonymous: the random app ID links one phone\'s samples, so under Brazil\'s data protection law (LGPD) they are personal data.

The public map, not online yet, will be anonymous. It will show only totals per small area (hexagons about 50 m across) and carrier: signal strength, network type, how often there was service, emergency calls only or no service, and the month last seen. No app ID, recording, exact time or exact point will be published. A random 300 to 800 m or more will be left out around where each recording starts and ends, and around where you stop before really setting off. An area seen by only one phone will appear only in a monthly batch, so a lone visit shows as “some time that month”.
Logging needs precise location. Allow precise location for this app in Settings.
Logging needs location access. Allow location for this app in Settings.
Logging needs phone access to read your SIM. Allow Phone for this app in Settings.
